`python3 budget.py 2026-09` now counts only September's transactions, and running it with no argument gives the same all-transactions totals as before.

I ran it against your data:

| Envelope | No month (all) | `2026-08` | `2026-09` |
|---|---|---|---|
| groceries | 174.60 | 403.05 | 371.55 |
| fuel | 22.85 | 78.10 | 124.75 |
| eating out | 45.75 | 111.50 | 84.25 |
| household | 54.61 | 73.01 | 101.60 |

- **Month with no transactions:** a month like `2026-10` shows every envelope at its full allocation rather than an error.
- **Bad input:** anything that isn't a real `YYYY-MM` month (`2026-13`, `sept`, `2026-9`) or more than one argument prints a message to stderr and exits with status 2.

The change is all in `budget.py`: two small helpers (`parse_month`, `in_month`) and the argument handling in `main`, plus the usage line in the docstring.
